请输出当前步骤的 <think>, <report> 和 <action> (仅输出XML标签)：

<think>
上一轮行动使用了jina_search，搜索关键词是"26岁开始做专职导演 65岁之后不再拍戏 享年89岁 导演"。搜索结果主要指向Instagram上的热门话题或视频，这些结果看起来像是社交媒体上的标签或帖子，而不是可靠的传记信息。搜索结果没有提供具体的导演姓名，只是重复了问题中的描述。这表明直接搜索问题描述可能无法找到答案，因为问题本身可能是一个谜题或特定知识。

我需要调整策略。与其搜索整个描述，不如尝试搜索更具体的组合，或者寻找符合这些年龄特征的知名导演。条件包括：
1. 26岁开始做专职导演，当年写出第一个电影剧本。
2. 65岁之后不再作为导演拍戏。
3. 享年89岁。

这意味着这位导演出生于某年，26岁开始导演生涯，65岁退休，89岁去世。我可以计算一下可能的出生年份。假设导演在26岁开始导演生涯，65岁退休，那么导演生涯持续了39年（65-26）。如果享年89岁，那么他/她可能在89岁时去世。

我可以尝试搜索"享年89岁 导演 65岁退休"或"26岁开始导演 第一个剧本"。但更好的方法是先列出一些符合年龄条件的知名导演，然后验证细节。

一些可能符合的导演：
- 黑泽明（Akira Kurosawa）：生于1910年，卒于1998年（享年88岁），不符合89岁。
- 英格玛·伯格曼（Ingmar Bergman）：生于1918年，卒于2007年（享年89岁）。他26岁开始导演生涯吗？伯格曼在1944年执导了第一部电影《危机》（Crisis），当时他26岁（生于1918年，1944年时26岁）。他写出第一个电影剧本吗？他早期是编剧，但第一个电影剧本可能是《危机》的剧本？他65岁之后不再执导电影吗？伯格曼在1983年执导了《芬妮与亚历山大》（Fanny and Alexander），当时他65岁（1983-1918=65）。之后他退休了，不再执导电影，专注于写作和绘画。他于2007年去世，享年89岁。这完全符合条件！

让我验证一下：
- 英格玛·伯格曼（Ingmar Bergman）：瑞典导演。
- 出生：1918年7月14日。
- 26岁：1944年，他执导了第一部电影《危机》（Crisis），并编写了剧本？实际上，伯格曼在1944年与导演古斯塔夫·莫兰德尔（Gustaf Molander）合作编写了《危机》的剧本，但他是联合编剧。他是否"当年写出了第一个电影剧本"？他早期是编剧，但第一个电影剧本可能是《危机》。需要确认。

**Ernst Ingmar Bergman**[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-1) (14 July 1918 – 30 July 2007) was a Swedish film and theatre director and screenwriter. He is considered one of the greatest and most important filmmakers in the [history of cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_cinema "History of cinema"), most notably as a prominent figure of both European film industry and [Swedish cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema_of_Sweden "Cinema of Sweden"). His films have been described as "profoundly personal meditations into the myriad struggles facing the psyche and the soul."[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-2)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-3)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-4)

Among his most acclaimed works are _[The Seventh Seal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Seventh\_Seal "The Seventh Seal")_ (1957), _[Wild Strawberries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wild\_Strawberries\_(film) "Wild Strawberries (film)")_ (1957), _[Persona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persona\_(1966\_film) "Persona (1966 film)")_ (1966) and _[Fanny and Alexander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fanny\_and\_Alexander "Fanny and Alexander")_ (1982), which were included in the [2012 edition of _Sight & Sound_'s Greatest Films of All Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sight_and_Sound_Greatest_Films_of_All_Time_2012 "The Sight and Sound Greatest Films of All Time 2012").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-5) He was also ranked No. 8 on the magazine's 2002 "Greatest Directors of All Time" list.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-6) Other notable works include _[Sawdust and Tinsel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sawdust\_and\_Tinsel "Sawdust and Tinsel")_ (1953), _[A Lesson in Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Lesson\_in\_Love\_(1954\_film) "A Lesson in Love (1954 film)")_ (1954), _[Smiles of a Summer Night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smiles\_of\_a\_Summer\_Night "Smiles of a Summer Night")_ (1955), _[The Virgin Spring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Virgin\_Spring "The Virgin Spring")_ (1960), _[Through a Glass Darkly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Through\_a\_Glass\_Darkly\_(film) "Through a Glass Darkly (film)")_ (1961), _[Winter Light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winter\_Light "Winter Light")_ and _[The Silence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Silence\_(1963\_film) "The Silence (1963 film)")_ (both 1963), _[Shame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shame\_(1968\_film) "Shame (1968 film)")_ (1968) which was called the director's ultimate personal vision of war,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-:1-7)_[Cries and Whispers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cries\_and\_Whispers "Cries and Whispers")_ (1972), _[Scenes from a Marriage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scenes\_from\_a\_Marriage "Scenes from a Marriage")_ (1973) and _[Autumn Sonata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autumn\_Sonata "Autumn Sonata")_ (1978). His films led to international acclaim and garnered [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards") wins and nominations throughout his career, including his personal [Irving G. Thalberg Memorial Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irving_G._Thalberg_Memorial_Award "Irving G. Thalberg Memorial Award") and three competitive wins accepted for [Best Foreign Language Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_International_Feature_Film "Academy Award for Best International Feature Film") to [Swedish entries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Swedish_submissions_for_the_Academy_Award_for_Best_International_Feature_Film "List of Swedish submissions for the Academy Award for Best International Feature Film").

Bergman directed more than 60 films and documentaries, most of which he also wrote, for both cinema releases and television screenings. Most of his films were set in Sweden, and many of his films from 1961 onward were filmed on the island of [Fårö](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F%C3%A5r%C3%B6 "Fårö"). He forged a creative partnership with his cinematographers [Gunnar Fischer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gunnar_Fischer "Gunnar Fischer") and [Sven Nykvist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sven_Nykvist "Sven Nykvist"). Bergman also had a theatrical career that included periods as Leading Director of Sweden's [Royal Dramatic Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Dramatic_Theatre "Royal Dramatic Theatre") in Stockholm and of Germany's [Residenztheater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Residenztheater "Residenztheater") in Munich.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-8) He directed more than 170 plays. Among his company of actors were [Harriet Andersson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harriet_Andersson "Harriet Andersson"), [Bibi Andersson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bibi_Andersson "Bibi Andersson"), [Liv Ullmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liv_Ullmann "Liv Ullmann"), [Gunnar Björnstrand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gunnar_Bj%C3%B6rnstrand "Gunnar Björnstrand"), [Erland Josephson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erland_Josephson "Erland Josephson"), [Ingrid Thulin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingrid_Thulin "Ingrid Thulin"), [Gunnel Lindblom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gunnel_Lindblom "Gunnel Lindblom") and [Max von Sydow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_von_Sydow "Max von Sydow").

## Biography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ingmar_Bergman&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Biography")]

### Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ingmar_Bergman&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early life")]

Ernst Ingmar Bergman was born in [Uppsala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uppsala "Uppsala") on 14 July 1918,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-FOOTNOTESteene200523-9) the son of nurse Karin ([née](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birth_name#Maiden_and_married_names "Birth name")Åkerblom) and [Lutheran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lutheranism "Lutheranism") minister (and later chaplain to the [King of Sweden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monarch_of_Sweden "Monarch of Sweden")) [Erik Bergman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erik_Bergman_(Lutheran_minister) "Erik Bergman (Lutheran minister)"). His mother was of [Walloon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walloon_immigration_to_Sweden "Walloon immigration to Sweden") descent.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGado1986374-10)[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-13) The Bergman family was originally from [Järvsö](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%A4rvs%C3%B6 "Järvsö"). On his father's side, Bergman was a descendant of the noble Bröms, Ehrenskiöld, and [Stockenström](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockenstr%C3%B6m "Stockenström") clergy families of Finnish, German, and Swedish origin. His father also descended from the German noble families [Flach](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Flach_(noble_family)&action=edit&redlink=1 "Flach (noble family) (page does not exist)")[[sv](https://sv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flach "sv:Flach")] and de Frese introduced at the Swedish [Riddarhuset](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riddarhuset "Riddarhuset"). Bergman's paternal grandmother and maternal grandfather were cousins, making his parents second cousins. On his mother's side, he was descended from Dutch merchant Paul Calwagen, who left Holland for Sweden in the 17th century; Paul's Dutch-Swedish wife, Maria van der Hagen, was a descendant of the court painter Laurens van der Plas. Bergman's mother was also a descendant of the noble Tigerschiöld and Weinholz families, as well as the [Bure](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bure_(noble_family)&action=edit&redlink=1 "Bure (noble family) (page does not exist)")[[sv](https://sv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bure_(adlig_sl%C3%A4kt) "sv:Bure (adlig släkt)")] family.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

[![Image 6](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/eb/Ingmar_86135a.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ingmar_86135a.jpg)

Bergman as a young man

Bergman grew up with his older brother [Dag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dag_Bergman "Dag Bergman") and younger sister [Margareta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margareta_Bergman "Margareta Bergman") surrounded by [religious imagery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Religious_image "Religious image") and discussion. His father was a conservative parish minister with strict ideas of parenting. Ingmar was locked up in dark closets for infractions such as wetting himself. "While father preached away in the pulpit and the congregation prayed, sang, or listened", Ingmar wrote in his autobiography _Laterna Magica_, "I devoted my interest to the church's mysterious world of low arches, thick walls, the smell of [eternity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eternity "Eternity"), the coloured sunlight quivering above the strangest vegetation of [medieval paintings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medieval_painting "Medieval painting") and carved figures on ceilings and walls. There was everything that one's imagination could desire—[angels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angel "Angel"), [saints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint "Saint"), dragons, [prophets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prophet "Prophet"), devils, humans..." Although raised in a devout [Lutheran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lutheran "Lutheran") household, Bergman later stated that he lost his faith at age eight, and came to terms with this fact while making _[Winter Light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winter\_Light "Winter Light")_ in 1962.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-14) His interest in theatre and film began early; at the age of nine, he traded a set of [tin soldiers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tin_soldier "Tin soldier") for a [magic lantern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic_lantern "Magic lantern"). Within a year, he had created a private world by playing with this toy in which he felt completely at home. He fashioned his own scenery, [marionettes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marionette "Marionette"), and lighting effects and gave puppet productions of [Strindberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/August_Strindberg "August Strindberg") plays in which he spoke all the parts."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-15)[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-16)

Bergman attended the [Palmgren School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palmgrenska_samskolan "Palmgrenska samskolan") as a teenager. His school years were unhappy,[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-FOOTNOTESteene200533-17) and he remembered them unfavourably in later years. In a 1944 letter concerning the film _[Torment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torment\_(1944\_film) "Torment (1944 film)")_ (sometimes known as _Frenzy_), which sparked debate on the condition of Swedish high schools (and which Bergman had written),[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGado198659-18) the school's principal Henning Håkanson wrote, among other things, that Bergman had been a "problem child".[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-19) Bergman wrote in a response that he had strongly disliked the emphasis on homework and testing in his formal schooling.

In 1934, aged 16, he was sent to Germany to spend the summer holidays with family friends. He attended a [Nazi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NSDAP "NSDAP") rally in [Weimar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weimar "Weimar") at which he saw [Adolf Hitler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adolf_Hitler "Adolf Hitler").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-20) He later wrote in _Laterna Magica_ (_The Magic Lantern_) about the visit to Germany, describing how the German family had put a portrait of Hitler on the wall by his bed, and that "for many years, I was on Hitler's side, delighted by his success and saddened by his defeats".[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-21) Bergman commented that "Hitler was unbelievably [charismatic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charisma "Charisma"). He electrified the crowd. ... The [Nazism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazism "Nazism") I had seen seemed fun and youthful."[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-:0-22) Bergman did two five-month stretches of mandatory military service in Sweden.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-23) He later reflected,

> When the doors to the concentration camps were thrown open, at first I did not want to believe my eyes ... When the truth came out it was a hideous shock for me. In a brutal and violent way I was suddenly ripped of my innocence.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-:0-22)

Bergman enrolled at Stockholm University College (later renamed [Stockholm University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm_University "Stockholm University")) in 1937, to study art and literature. He spent most of his time involved in student theatre and became a "genuine movie addict".[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-24) At the same time, a romantic involvement led to a physical confrontation with his father which resulted in a break in their relationship which lasted for many years. Although he did not graduate from the university, he wrote a number of plays and an opera, and became an assistant director at a local theatre. In 1942, he was given the opportunity to direct one of his own scripts, _Caspar's Death_. The play was seen by members of [Svensk Filmindustri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AB_Svensk_Filmindustri "AB Svensk Filmindustri"), which then offered Bergman a position working on scripts. He married [Else Fisher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Else_Fisher "Else Fisher") in 1943.

### Film career until 1975

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ingmar_Bergman&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Film career until 1975")]

[![Image 7](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4b/Ingmar_Bergman_Smultronstallet.jpg/250px-Ingmar_Bergman_Smultronstallet.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ingmar_Bergman_Smultronstallet.jpg)

Bergman in 1957

Bergman's film career began in 1941 with his work rewriting scripts, but his first major accomplishment was in 1944 when he wrote the screenplay for _[Torment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torment\_(1944\_film) "Torment (1944 film)")_ (a.k.a. _Frenzy_) (_Hets_), a film directed by [Alf Sjöberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alf_Sj%C3%B6berg "Alf Sjöberg"). Along with writing the screenplay, he was also appointed assistant director of the film. In his second autobiographical book, _Images: My Life in Film_, Bergman describes the filming of the exteriors as his actual film directorial debut.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-25) The film sparked debate on Swedish formal education. When Henning Håkanson (the principal of the high school Bergman had attended) wrote a letter following the film's release, Bergman, according to scholar Frank Gado, disparaged in a response what he viewed as Håkanson's implication that students "who did not fit some arbitrary prescription of worthiness deserved the system's cruel neglect".[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGado198659-18) Bergman also stated in the letter that he "hated school as a principle, as a system and as an institution. And as such I have definitely not wanted to criticize my own school, but all schools."[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-26)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-27) The international success of this film led to Bergman's first opportunity to direct a year later. During the next ten years he wrote and directed more than a dozen films, including _[Prison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prison\_(1949\_film) "Prison (1949 film)")_ (_Fängelse_) in 1949, as well as _[Sawdust and Tinsel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sawdust\_and\_Tinsel "Sawdust and Tinsel")_ (_Gycklarnas afton_) and _[Summer with Monika](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer\_with\_Monika "Summer with Monika")_ (_Sommaren med Monika_), both released in 1953.

[![Image 8](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/70/Bergman_Sjostrom_1957.jpg/330px-Bergman_Sjostrom_1957.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bergman_Sjostrom_1957.jpg)

 Bergman and [Victor Sjöström](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m "Victor Sjöström") on the set of _[Wild Strawberries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wild\_Strawberries\_(film) "Wild Strawberries (film)")_ (1957)

Bergman first achieved worldwide success with _[Smiles of a Summer Night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smiles\_of\_a\_Summer\_Night "Smiles of a Summer Night")_ (_Sommarnattens leende_, 1955), which won for "Best poetic humour" and was nominated for the [Palme d'Or](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palme_d%27Or "Palme d'Or") at Cannes the following year. This was followed by _[The Seventh Seal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Seventh\_Seal "The Seventh Seal")_ (_Det sjunde inseglet_) and _[Wild Strawberries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wild\_Strawberries\_(film) "Wild Strawberries (film)")_ (_Smultronstället_), released in Sweden ten months apart in 1957. _The Seventh Seal_ won a special jury prize and was nominated for the Palme d'Or at Cannes, and _Wild Strawberries_ won numerous awards for Bergman and its star, [Victor Sjöström](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Sj%C3%B6str%C3%B6m "Victor Sjöström"). Bergman continued to be productive for the next two decades. From the early 1960s, he spent much of his life on the island of [Fårö](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F%C3%A5r%C3%B6 "Fårö"), where he made several films.

In the early 1960s he directed three films that explored the theme of faith and doubt in God, _[Through a Glass Darkly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Through\_a\_Glass\_Darkly\_(film) "Through a Glass Darkly (film)")_ (_Såsom i en Spegel_, 1961), _[Winter Light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winter\_Light "Winter Light")_ (_Nattvardsgästerna_, 1962), and _[The Silence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Silence\_(1963\_film) "The Silence (1963 film)")_ (_Tystnaden_, 1963). Critics created the notion that the common themes in these three films made them a trilogy or cinematic [triptych](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triptych "Triptych"). Bergman initially responded that he did not plan these three films as a trilogy, and that he could not see any common motifs in them, but he later seemed to adopt the notion, with some equivocation.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-28)[[d]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-29) His parody of the films of [Federico Fellini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Fellini "Federico Fellini"), _[All These Women](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All\_These\_Women "All These Women")_ (_För att inte tala om alla dessa kvinnor_) was released in 1964.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-30)

_[Persona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persona\_(1966\_film) "Persona (1966 film)")_ (1966), starring Bibi Andersson and Liv Ullmann, is a film Bergman considered one of his most important works. While the highly experimental film won few awards, it has been considered his masterpiece. Other films of the period include _[The Virgin Spring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Virgin\_Spring "The Virgin Spring")_ (_Jungfrukällan_, 1960), _[Hour of the Wolf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hour\_of\_the\_Wolf "Hour of the Wolf")_ (_Vargtimmen_, 1968), _[Shame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shame\_(1968\_film) "Shame (1968 film)")_ (_Skammen_, 1968) and _[The Passion of Anna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Passion\_of\_Anna "The Passion of Anna")_ (_En Passion_, 1969). With his cinematographer [Sven Nykvist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sven_Nykvist "Sven Nykvist"), Bergman made use of a crimson color scheme for _[Cries and Whispers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cries\_and\_Whispers "Cries and Whispers")_ (1972), which received a nomination for the [Academy Award for Best Picture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/46th_Academy_Awards "46th Academy Awards").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-31) He also produced extensively for Swedish television at this time. Two works of note were _[Scenes from a Marriage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scenes\_from\_a\_Marriage "Scenes from a Marriage")_ (_Scener ur ett äktenskap_, 1973) and _[The Magic Flute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Magic\_Flute\_(1975\_film) "The Magic Flute (1975 film)")_ (_Trollflöjten_, 1975).

[![Image 9](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/84/Ingmar_Bergman_%26_Sven_Nykvist.jpg/330px-Ingmar_Bergman_%26_Sven_Nykvist.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ingmar_Bergman_%26_Sven_Nykvist.jpg)

Bergman with his long-time cinematographer [Sven Nykvist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sven_Nykvist "Sven Nykvist") during the production of _[Through a Glass Darkly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Through\_a\_Glass\_Darkly\_(film) "Through a Glass Darkly (film)")_ (1960)

### Tax evasion charges in 1976

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ingmar_Bergman&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Tax evasion charges in 1976")]

On 30 January 1976, while rehearsing [August Strindberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/August_Strindberg "August Strindberg")'s _[The Dance of Death](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Dance\_of\_Death\_(Strindberg) "The Dance of Death (Strindberg)")_ at the [Royal Dramatic Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Dramatic_Theatre "Royal Dramatic Theatre") in Stockholm, he was arrested by two plainclothes police officers and charged with income tax evasion. The impact on Bergman was devastating. He suffered a nervous breakdown as a result of the humiliation, and was hospitalised in a state of deep depression.

The investigation focused on an alleged 1970 transaction of 500,000 [Swedish kronor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swedish_kronor "Swedish kronor") (SEK) between Bergman's Swedish company _Cinematograf_ and its Swiss subsidiary _Persona_, an entity that was mainly used for the paying of salaries to foreign actors. Bergman dissolved _Persona_ in 1974 after having been notified by the Swedish Central Bank and subsequently reported the income. On 23 March 1976, the special prosecutor Anders Nordenadler dropped the charges against Bergman, saying that the alleged crime had no legal basis, and added that it would be like bringing "charges against a person who has stolen his own car, thinking it was someone else's".[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-32) Director General Gösta S Ekman, chief of the Swedish Internal Revenue Service, defended the failed investigation, saying that the investigation was dealing with important legal material, and that Bergman was treated just like any other suspect. He expressed regret that Bergman had left the country, hoping that Bergman was a "stronger" person now when the investigation had shown that he had not done any wrong.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-33)

Although the charges were dropped, Bergman became disconsolate, fearing he would never again return to directing. Despite pleas by the Swedish prime minister [Olof Palme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olof_Palme "Olof Palme"), high public figures, and leaders of the film industry, he vowed never to work in Sweden again. He closed down his studio on the island of [Fårö](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F%C3%A5r%C3%B6 "Fårö"), suspended two announced film projects, and went into self-imposed exile in [Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munich "Munich"), [West Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Germany "West Germany"). [Harry Schein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Schein "Harry Schein"), director of the [Swedish Film Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swedish_Film_Institute "Swedish Film Institute"), estimated the immediate damage as ten million SEK and hundreds of jobs lost.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-34)

### Aftermath following arrest

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ingmar_Bergman&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Aftermath following arrest")]

Bergman then briefly considered the possibility of working in America. His next film, _[The Serpent's Egg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Serpent%27s\_Egg\_(film) "The Serpent's Egg (film)")_ (1977) was a West German-U.S. production and was his second English-language film (the first being _[The Touch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Touch\_(1971\_film) "The Touch (1971 film)")_, 1971). This was followed by a British-Norwegian co-production, _[Autumn Sonata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autumn\_Sonata "Autumn Sonata")_ (_Höstsonaten_, 1978) starring [Ingrid Bergman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingrid_Bergman "Ingrid Bergman") (no relation) and [Liv Ullmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liv_Ullmann "Liv Ullmann"), and _[From the Life of the Marionettes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/From\_the\_Life\_of\_the\_Marionettes "From the Life of the Marionettes")_ (_Aus dem Leben der Marionetten_, 1980) which was a British-West German co-production.

He temporarily returned to his homeland to direct _[Fanny and Alexander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fanny\_and\_Alexander "Fanny and Alexander")_ (_Fanny och Alexander_, 1982). Bergman stated that the film would be his last, and that afterwards he would focus on directing theatre. After that he wrote several film scripts and directed a number of television specials. As with previous work for television, some of these productions were later theatrically released. The last such work was _[Saraband](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saraband "Saraband")_ (2003), a sequel to _Scenes from a Marriage_. It was directed by Bergman when he was 84 years old.

Although he continued to operate from Munich, by mid-1978 Bergman had overcome some of his bitterness toward the Swedish government. In July of that year he visited Sweden, celebrating his sixtieth birthday on the island of Fårö, and partly resumed his work as a director at Royal Dramatic Theatre. To honour his return, the [Swedish Film Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swedish_Film_Institute "Swedish Film Institute") launched a new [Ingmar Bergman Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman_Award "Ingmar Bergman Award") to be awarded annually for excellence in filmmaking.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-35) Still, he remained in Munich until 1984. In one of his last major interviews, conducted in 2005 on the island of [Fårö](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F%C3%A5r%C3%B6 "Fårö"), Bergman said that despite being active during the exile, he had effectively lost eight years of his professional life.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-36)

### Retirement and death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ingmar_Bergman&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Retirement and death")]

[![Image 10](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f0/Grave_of_Ingmar_Bergman%2C_may_2008.jpg/330px-Grave_of_Ingmar_Bergman%2C_may_2008.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Grave_of_Ingmar_Bergman,_may_2008.jpg)

The grave of Bergman and his last wife Ingrid.

Bergman retired from filmmaking in December 2003. He had hip surgery in October 2006 and was making a difficult recovery. He died in his sleep[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-37) at age 89; his body was found at his home on the island of Fårö, on 30 July 2007.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-38) It was the same day another renowned existentialist film director, [Michelangelo Antonioni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelangelo_Antonioni "Michelangelo Antonioni"), died. The interment was private, at the [Fårö Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F%C3%A5r%C3%B6_Church "Fårö Church") on 18 August 2007. A place in the Fårö churchyard was prepared for him under heavy secrecy. Although he was buried on the island of Fårö, his name and date of birth were inscribed under his wife's name on a tomb at Roslagsbro churchyard, [Norrtälje Municipality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norrt%C3%A4lje_Municipality "Norrtälje Municipality"), several years before his death.

## Style of working

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ingmar_Bergman&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Style of working")]

### Repertory company

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ingmar_Bergman&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Repertory company")]

[![Image 11](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/76/Ingmar_Bergman_and_Ingrid_Thulin_-Tystnaden.jpg/330px-Ingmar_Bergman_and_Ingrid_Thulin_-Tystnaden.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ingmar_Bergman_and_Ingrid_Thulin_-Tystnaden.jpg)

Bergman and actress [Ingrid Thulin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingrid_Thulin "Ingrid Thulin") during the production of _[The Silence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Silence\_(1963\_film) "The Silence (1963 film)")_, 1963

Bergman developed a personal "repertory company" of Swedish actors whom he repeatedly cast in his films, including Max von Sydow, Bibi Andersson, Harriet Andersson, [Erland Josephson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erland_Josephson "Erland Josephson"), Ingrid Thulin, [Gunnel Lindblom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gunnel_Lindblom "Gunnel Lindblom"), and Gunnar Björnstrand, each of whom appeared in at least five Bergman features. Norwegian actress Liv Ullmann, who appeared in nine of Bergman's films and one televisual film (_Saraband_), was the last to join this group (in the film _Persona_), and ultimately became the most closely associated with Bergman, both artistically and personally. They had a daughter together, [Linn Ullmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linn_Ullmann "Linn Ullmann") (born 1966).

In Bergman's working arrangement with Sven Nykvist, his best-known [cinematographer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinematographer "Cinematographer"), the two men developed sufficient rapport to allow Bergman not to worry about the composition of a shot until the day before it was filmed. On the morning of the shoot, he would briefly speak to Nykvist about the mood and composition he hoped for, and then leave Nykvist to work, lacking interruption or comment until post-production discussion of the next day's work.

### Financing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ingmar_Bergman&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Financing")]

[![Image 12](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/79/Filmstaden.jpg/330px-Filmstaden.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Filmstaden.jpg)

A great number of Bergman's interior scenes were filmed at the _[Filmstaden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmstaden "Filmstaden")_ studios north of Stockholm.

By Bergman's own account, he never had a problem with funding. He was one of the few film makers of the time who had managed to stay clear of international financing, working out his own techniques for funding films.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-:1-7) He cited two reasons for this: one, that he did not live in the United States, which he viewed as obsessed with box-office earnings; and two, that his films tended to be low-budget affairs. (_Cries and Whispers_, for instance, was finished for about $450,000, while _Scenes from a Marriage_, a six-episode television feature, cost only $200,000.)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-autogenerated1975-40)

### Technique

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ingmar_Bergman&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Technique")]

Bergman usually wrote his films' screenplays, thinking about them for months or years before starting the actual process of writing, which he viewed as somewhat tedious. His earlier films are carefully constructed and are either based on his plays or written in collaboration with other authors. Bergman stated that in his later works, when on occasion his actors would want to do things differently from his own intention, he would let them, noting that the results were often "disastrous" when he did not do so. As his career progressed, Bergman increasingly let his actors [improvise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Improvisation "Improvisation") their dialogue. In his later films, he wrote just the ideas informing the scene and allowed his actors to determine the exact dialogue. When viewing [daily rushes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daily_rushes "Daily rushes"), Bergman stressed the importance of being critical but unemotive, claiming that he asked himself not if the work was great or terrible, but rather if it was sufficient or needed to be reshot.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-autogenerated1975-40)

### Subjects

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ingmar_Bergman&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Subjects")]

Bergman's films usually deal with [existential](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Existentialism "Existentialism") questions of mortality, loneliness, and religious faith. In addition to these cerebral topics, however, sexual desire features in the foreground of most of his films, whether the central event is [medieval](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medieval "Medieval")[plague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plague_(disease) "Plague (disease)") (_[The Seventh Seal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Seventh\_Seal "The Seventh Seal")_), upper-class family activity in early twentieth century Uppsala (_[Fanny and Alexander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fanny\_and\_Alexander "Fanny and Alexander")_), or contemporary alienation (_[The Silence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Silence\_(1963\_film) "The Silence (1963 film)")_). His female characters are usually more in touch with their sexuality than their male equivalents, and unafraid to proclaim it, sometimes with breathtaking overtness (as in _[Cries and Whispers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cries\_and\_Whispers "Cries and Whispers")_) as would define the work of "the conjurer," as Bergman called himself in a 1960 _[TIME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time\_(magazine) "Time (magazine)")_ cover story.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-41) In an interview with _[Playboy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Playboy "Playboy")_ in 1964, he said: "The manifestation of sex is very important, and particularly to me, for above all, I don't want to make merely intellectual films. I want audiences to feel, to sense my films. This to me is much more important than their understanding them." Film, Bergman said, was his demanding mistress.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-42) While he was a [social democrat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_democracy "Social democracy") as an adult, Bergman stated that "as an artist I'm not politically involved ... I don't make propaganda for either one attitude or the other."[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-43)

### Bergman's views on his career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ingmar_Bergman&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Bergman's views on his career")]

When asked in the series of interviews later titled "Ingmar Bergman – 3 dokumentärer om film, teater, Fårö och livet" conducted by Marie Nyreröd for Swedish TV and released in 2004, Bergman said that of his works, he held _[Winter Light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winter\_Light "Winter Light")_,[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-44)_[Persona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persona\_(1966\_film) "Persona (1966 film)")_, and _[Cries and Whispers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cries\_and\_Whispers "Cries and Whispers")_[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-FOOTNOTESteene2005-45) in the highest regard. There he also states that he managed to push the envelope of film making in the films _Persona_ and _Cries and Whispers_. Bergman stated on numerous occasions (for example in the interview book _Bergman on Bergman_) that _The Silence_ meant the end of the era in which religious questions were a major concern of his films. Bergman said that he would get depressed by his own films: "jittery and ready to cry... and miserable."[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-46) In the same interview he also stated: "If there is one thing I miss about working with films, it is working with Sven" (Nykvist), the third cinematographer with whom he had collaborated.

### Theatrical work

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ingmar_Bergman&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Theatrical work")]

Main article: [List of stage productions directed by Ingmar Bergman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stage_productions_directed_by_Ingmar_Bergman "List of stage productions directed by Ingmar Bergman")

Although Bergman was universally famous for his contribution to cinema, he was also an active and productive stage director throughout his life. During his studies at what was then Stockholm University College, he became active in its student theatre, where he made a name for himself early on. His first work after graduation was as a trainee-director at a Stockholm theatre. At twenty-six years, he became the youngest theatrical manager in Europe at the [Helsingborg City Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helsingborg_City_Theatre "Helsingborg City Theatre"). He stayed at [Helsingborg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helsingborg "Helsingborg") for three years and then became the director at [Gothenburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gothenburg "Gothenburg") city theatre from 1946 to 1949.

He became director of the [Malmö City Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malm%C3%B6_City_Theatre "Malmö City Theatre") in 1953, and remained for seven years. Many of his star actors were people with whom he began working on stage. He was the director of the [Royal Dramatic Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Dramatic_Theatre "Royal Dramatic Theatre") in Stockholm from 1960 to 1966, and manager from 1963 to 1966, where he began a long-time collaboration with choreographer [Donya Feuer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donya_Feuer "Donya Feuer").

After Bergman left Sweden because of the tax evasion incident, he became director of the _[Residenz Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Residenz\_Theatre "Residenz Theatre")_ of [Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munich "Munich"), West Germany (1977–1984). He remained active in theatre throughout the 1990s and made his final production on stage with [Henrik Ibsen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henrik_Ibsen "Henrik Ibsen")'s _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts\_(play) "Ghosts (play)")_ at the [Brooklyn Academy of Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn_Academy_of_Music "Brooklyn Academy of Music") in 2003.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-47)

## Personal life

### Marriages and children

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ingmar_Bergman&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Marriages and children")]

[![Image 13](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fb/Kabi-Laretei-Ingmar-Bergman.jpg/250px-Kabi-Laretei-Ingmar-Bergman.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kabi-Laretei-Ingmar-Bergman.jpg)

Bergman with fourth wife, Estonian concert pianist [Käbi Laretei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%A4bi_Laretei "Käbi Laretei")

Bergman was married five times:

*   25 March 1943– 1945, to [Else Fisher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Else_Fisher "Else Fisher") (1 March 1918 – 3 March 2006), choreographer and dancer (divorced). Children: 
    *   Lena Bergman, actress, born 1943.

*   22 July 1945– 1950, to [Ellen Lundström](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ellen_Lundstr%C3%B6m&action=edit&redlink=1 "Ellen Lundström (page does not exist)") (23 April 1919 – 6 March 2007), choreographer and film director (divorced). Children: 
    *   [Eva Bergman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eva_Bergman "Eva Bergman"), film director, born 1945
    *   Jan Bergman, film director (1946–2000)
    *   the twins [Mats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mats_Bergman "Mats Bergman") and [Anna Bergman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anna_Bergman "Anna Bergman"), both actors and film directors, born in 1948.

*   1951– 1959, to [Gun Grut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gun_Bergman "Gun Bergman") (1916–1971), journalist (divorced). Children: 
    *   Ingmar Bergman Jr., retired airline captain, born 1951.

*   1959– 1969, to [Käbi Laretei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%A4bi_Laretei "Käbi Laretei") (14 July 1922 – 31 October 2014), [concert pianist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concert_pianist "Concert pianist") (divorced). Children: 
    *   [Daniel Bergman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Bergman "Daniel Bergman"), film director, born 1962.

*   11 November 1971– 20 May 1995, to Ingrid von Rosen (maiden name Karlebo, 17 January 1930 – 20 May 1995). Children: 
    *   Maria von Rosen, author, born 1959.

[![Image 14](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9c/Ullmann-Bergman-1968.jpeg/250px-Ullmann-Bergman-1968.jpeg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ullmann-Bergman-1968.jpeg)

Bergman with Norwegian actress [Liv Ullmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liv_Ullmann "Liv Ullmann") in 1968. The couple had a daughter, [Linn Ullmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linn_Ullmann "Linn Ullmann"), in 1966

The first four marriages ended in divorce, while the last ended when his wife Ingrid died of [stomach cancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stomach_cancer "Stomach cancer") in 1995, aged 65. Aside from his marriages, Bergman had romantic relationships with actresses Harriet Andersson (1952–1955), Bibi Andersson (1955–1959), and Liv Ullmann (1965–1970). He was the father of writer [Linn Ullmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linn_Ullmann "Linn Ullmann") with Ullmann. In all, Bergman had nine children, one of whom predeceased him. Bergman eventually married all the mothers of his children, with the exception of Liv Ullmann. His daughter with his last wife, Ingrid von Rosen, was born twelve years before their marriage. He had dozens of mistresses throughout his life and would justify the affairs to his various wives by telling them: "I have so many lives."[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-48)

Although Bergman once described himself as one who had lost his faith in an afterlife, in 2000 he stated that a conversation he had with Erland Josephson helped him to believe that he would see Ingrid again. He said, "I'm not actually afraid of dying. On the contrary, really. I think it'll be interesting."[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-49) In 2012, Max von Sydow stated to [Charlie Rose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie_Rose "Charlie Rose") that he had had many discussions with Bergman about religion which seemed to indicate that Bergman believed in an afterlife and von Sydow said that Bergman contacted him after his death to prove there was indeed a life after death, though he did not elaborate further.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-50)

In an early draft of his autobiography, Bergman said he raped his then-girlfriend [Karin Lannby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karin_Lannby "Karin Lannby"). The portion was edited out for the final version.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-51)[_[dubious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Accuracy\_dispute#Disputed\_statement "Wikipedia:Accuracy dispute") – [discuss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:Ingmar\_Bergman#Dubious "Talk:Ingmar Bergman")_]

### Health

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ingmar_Bergman&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Health")]

Bergman suffered from [insomnia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insomnia "Insomnia") and severe stomach problems dating back to childhood.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-52) He called his nervous stomach "a calamity as foolish as it is humiliating" and joked that the private lavatories he secured at the theatres in which he worked represented his "most lasting contribution to the history of theatre."[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-53)

## Awards and nominations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ingmar_Bergman&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Awards and nominations")]

In 1958, he won the [Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cannes_Film_Festival_Award_for_Best_Director "Cannes Film Festival Award for Best Director") award for _[Brink of Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brink\_of\_Life "Brink of Life")_ at the [Cannes Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1958_Cannes_Film_Festival "1958 Cannes Film Festival"),[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-54) and won the [Golden Bear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Bear "Golden Bear") for _[Wild Strawberries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wild\_Strawberries\_(film) "Wild Strawberries (film)")_ at the [Berlin International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/8th_Berlin_International_Film_Festival "8th Berlin International Film Festival").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-55) In 1960 Bergman was featured in the cover of _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time\_(magazine) "Time (magazine)")_, the first foreign-language filmmaker to do so since [Leni Riefenstahl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leni_Riefenstahl "Leni Riefenstahl") in 1936.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-56)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-57) In 1971, Bergman received the [Irving G. Thalberg Memorial Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irving_G._Thalberg_Memorial_Award "Irving G. Thalberg Memorial Award") at the [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/43rd_Academy_Awards "43rd Academy Awards") ceremony. Three of his films (_[The Virgin Spring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Virgin\_Spring "The Virgin Spring")_, _[Through a Glass Darkly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Through\_a\_Glass\_Darkly\_(film) "Through a Glass Darkly (film)")_, and _[Fanny and Alexander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fanny\_and\_Alexander "Fanny and Alexander")_) won the [Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Foreign_Language_Film "Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film"). In 1997, he was awarded the [Palme des Palmes (Palm of the Palms)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palme_d%27Or#Honorary_Palme_d'Or "Palme d'Or") at the [50th anniversary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997_Cannes_Film_Festival "1997 Cannes Film Festival") of the [Cannes Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cannes_Film_Festival "Cannes Film Festival"). He won many other awards and has been nominated for numerous other awards.

## Legacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ingmar_Bergman&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Legacy")]

See also: [List of accolades and awards received by Ingmar Bergman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_accolades_and_awards_received_by_Ingmar_Bergman "List of accolades and awards received by Ingmar Bergman") and [The Dove (1968 film)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dove_(1968_film) "The Dove (1968 film)")

[![Image 15](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f3/Popiersie_Ingmar_Bergman_ssj_20110627.jpg/250px-Popiersie_Ingmar_Bergman_ssj_20110627.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Popiersie_Ingmar_Bergman_ssj_20110627.jpg)

A bust of Bergman in Celebrity Alley in [Kielce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kielce "Kielce"), Poland

In 1996, _[Entertainment Weekly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entertainment\_Weekly "Entertainment Weekly")_ ranked Bergman at No. 8 in its "50 Greatest Directors" list.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-auto-58)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-59) In 2002, Bergman was listed at number nine on the [British Film Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Film_Institute "British Film Institute")'s _[Sight & Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sight\_%26\_Sound "Sight & Sound")_ list of the top ten film directors of modern times.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-60)[MovieMaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MovieMaker "MovieMaker") magazine ranked Bergman at No. 13 on their 2002 list of _The 25 Most Influential Directors of All Time_.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-61) Bergman was ranked at No. 36 on [Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire_(film_magazine) "Empire (film magazine)") magazine's "Top 40 Greatest Directors of All-Time" list in 2005.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-auto-58) In 2007, _[Total Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total\_Film "Total Film")_ magazine ranked Bergman at No. 7 on its "100 Greatest Film Directors Ever" list.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-62) In 2017, _[New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_York\_(magazine) "New York (magazine)")_ magazine ranked Bergman at number 55 on their list of _The 100 Best Screenwriters of All Time_.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-63)

[Stanley Kubrick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Kubrick "Stanley Kubrick") admired the work of Bergman and expressed it in personal letter: "Your vision of life has moved me deeply, much more deeply than I have ever been moved by any films. I believe you are the greatest film-maker at work today [...], unsurpassed by anyone in the creation of mood and atmosphere, the subtlety of performance, the avoidance of the obvious, the truthfulness and completeness of characterization. To this one must also add everything else that goes into the making of a film; [...] and I shall look forward with eagerness to each of your films."[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-64) Film critic [Philip French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_French "Philip French") referred to Bergman as "one of the greatest artists of the 20th century ... he found in literature and the performing arts a way of both recreating and questioning the [human condition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_condition "Human condition")."[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-65) Director [Martin Scorsese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Scorsese "Martin Scorsese") commented that "it's impossible to overestimate the effect that [his] films had on people."[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-66)[Terrence Rafferty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terrence_Rafferty "Terrence Rafferty") of _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_ wrote that throughout the 1960s, when Bergman "was considered pretty much the last word in cinematic profundity, his every tic was scrupulously pored over, analyzed, elaborated in ingenious arguments about identity, the nature of film, the fate of the artist in the modern world and so on."[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-67)

Bergman's work was a point of reference and inspiration for director [Woody Allen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woody_Allen "Woody Allen"). He described Bergman as "probably the greatest film artist, all things considered, since the invention of the motion picture camera".[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-68) Bergman's films are mentioned and praised in _[Annie Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annie\_Hall "Annie Hall")_ and other Allen films. Allen also admired Bergman's longtime director of photography [Sven Nykvist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sven_Nykvist "Sven Nykvist") and invited him to return as his DP on _[Crimes and Misdemeanors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crimes\_and\_Misdemeanors "Crimes and Misdemeanors")_.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-69) Danish Director [Thomas Vinterberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Vinterberg "Thomas Vinterberg") has cited Bergman as one of his major influences, "Bergman is always in my head. He is part of my upbringing and I was fortunate to meet him and get advice from him."[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-70)[Todd Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Todd_Field "Todd Field"), in an essay he wrote for the [Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Times "Los Angeles Times"), recalled Bergman toward the end of his life inviting Field and his wife to a production he directed of [Henrik Ibsen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henrik_Ibsen "Henrik Ibsen")’s _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts\_(play) "Ghosts (play)")_, and the influence this had on him. “Bergman belonged to all of us. He was our tunnel man building the aqueducts of our cinematic collective unconscious. Supplying water to a people who heretofore didn’t know they were thirsty.”[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-71)

Writer and director [Richard Ayoade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Ayoade "Richard Ayoade") counts Bergman as one of his inspirations. In 2017, the [British Film Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Film_Institute "British Film Institute") (BFI) hosted an Ingmar Bergman season and Ayoade said in a _[Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian "The Guardian")_ interview that he saw everything in it, "which was one of the best two months ever."[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-72) The BFI's programme included a discussion with Ayoade on Bergman's 1966 film, _[Persona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persona\_(1966\_film) "Persona (1966 film)")_, before a screening.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-73)[Bertrand Tavernier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bertrand_Tavernier "Bertrand Tavernier") said: "Bergman was the first to bring metaphysics– religion, death, existentialism– to the screen. But the best of Bergman is the way he speaks of women, of the relationship between men and women. He's like a miner digging in search of purity."[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-NYTObit-74)

After Bergman died, a large archive of notes was donated to the [Swedish Film Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swedish_Film_Institute "Swedish Film Institute"). Among the notes are several unpublished and unfinished scripts both for stage and films, and many more ideas for works in different stages of development. A never-performed play has the title _Kärlek utan älskare_ ("Love without lovers"), and has the note "Complete disaster!" written on the envelope; the play is about a director who disappears and an editor who tries to complete a work he has left unfinished. Other canceled projects include the script for a pornographic film which Bergman abandoned since he did not think it was alive enough, a play about a cannibal, some loose scenes set inside a womb, a film about the life of Jesus, a film about _[The Merry Widow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Merry\_Widow "The Merry Widow")_, and a play with the title _Från sperm till spöke_ ("From sperm to spook").[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-ratadetexter-75) The Swedish director Marcus Lindeen went through the material, and inspired by _Kärlek utan älskare_ he took samples from many of the works and turned them into a play, titled _[Arkivet för orealiserbara drömmar och visioner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arkivet\_f%C3%B6r\_orealiserbara\_dr%C3%B6mmar\_och\_visioner "Arkivet för orealiserbara drömmar och visioner")_ ("The archive for unrealisable dreams and visions"). Lindeen's play premiered on 27 May 2012 at the [Stockholm City Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm_City_Theatre "Stockholm City Theatre").[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-ratadetexter-75)

In 2018, in honor of Bergman's 100th birthday, [The Criterion Collection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Criterion_Collection "The Criterion Collection") compiled and released a [Blu-ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blu-ray "Blu-ray") disc [box set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boxed_set "Boxed set") comprising 39 of Bergman's features. The set spans Bergman's early career, beginning in the 1940s, up to his final film in 2003. The films are organized non-chronologically, and are instead presented in four groupings that mimic the procession of a film festival. Accompanying the discs is a book featuring critical essays on each of the films, intended to guide the viewer through the experience. Upon its release, _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_ critic Glenn Kenny assessed the set as "impressive and almost exhaustive", and interpreted it as "a fresh case for [Bergman's] continuing importance", in response to criticisms such as [Jonathan Rosenbaum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Rosenbaum "Jonathan Rosenbaum")'s 2007 opinion piece "Scenes From an Overrated Career".[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-76)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-77)

The [Ingmar Bergman International Debut Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman_International_Debut_Award "Ingmar Bergman International Debut Award") is awarded annually at the [Gothenburg Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gothenburg_Film_Festival "Gothenburg Film Festival"), in partnership with the Ingmar Bergman Foundation, the Bergman Estate and the Bergman Center on Fårö. The prize includes a visit to the Bergman Estate as well as to Bergmans personal archive in Stockholm.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_note-prizes2022-78)

3.   **[^](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_ref-16)**For an extended discussion of the profound influence that August Strindberg's work played in Bergman's life and career, see: Ottiliana Rolandsson, _Pure Artistry: Ingmar Bergman, the Face as Portal and the Performance of the Soul_, Ph.D. dissertation, University of California, Santa Barbara, 2010, especially chapter 3, "Bergman, Strindberg and the Territories of Imagination".
4.   **[^](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar_Bergman#cite_ref-29)**In contrast, in 1964 Bergman had the three scripts published in a single volume: "These three films deal with reduction. _Through a Glass Darkly_– conquered certainty. _Winter Light_– penetrated certainty. _The Silence_– God's silence— the negative imprint. Therefore, they constitute a trilogy." [The Criterion Collection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Criterion_Collection "The Criterion Collection") groups the films as a trilogy in a [boxed set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boxed_set "Boxed set"). In the 1963 documentary _[Ingmar Bergman Makes a Movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingmar\_Bergman\_Makes\_a\_Movie "Ingmar Bergman Makes a Movie")_, about the making of _Winter Light_, supports the idea that Bergman did not plan a trilogy. In the interview with Bergman about writing the script of _Winter Light_, and the interviews made during the shooting of it, he hardly mentions _[Through a Glass Darkly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Through\_a\_Glass\_Darkly\_(film) "Through a Glass Darkly (film)")_. Instead, he discusses the themes of _Winter Light_, in particular the religious issues, in relation to _[The Virgin Spring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Virgin\_Spring "The Virgin Spring")_.
